title: Determination of an efficient and reliable method for PCR detection of borrelial DNA from engorged ticks
author: Ušanović, Lejla
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Analyze PCR amplification results
steps.instruction: Figure 2. Results of PCR amplification – A1. Efficient PCR with clear band of 250bp presented as successful amplification, determined by using a positive control; All amplified bands with sizes differing from the positive control were defined as non-specific alleles; Four types of different PCR results: A2. Non-specific alleles; A3. Poor amplification; A4. A combination of poor amplification and non-specific alleles; B. Unsuccessful amplification detected in paired DNA extraction, after using DNA obtained from mouthparts (B1), whereas target region was amplified for the same sample but using DNA obtained from a part of scutum (B2); a 50 bp DNA ladder (BioLabs, New England) (A, B).

substeps.instruction: Identify clear band of 250bp as successful amplification using positive control
Define all amplified bands differing from positive control as non-specific alleles
Categorize PCR results into four types: Non-specific alleles, Poor amplification, Combination of poor amplification and non-specific alleles
Detect unsuccessful amplification in paired DNA extraction using DNA from mouthparts
Confirm target region amplified using DNA from part of scutum
Use 50 bp DNA ladder (BioLabs, New England) for size reference
